topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's themes on cancer evolution, the cell of origin, and the tumor microenvironment, outlining the core learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic mutations and epigenetic disruption in cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stepwise genetic mutation accumulation, clonal selection, and transient epigenetic disruptions drive neoplastic transformation and competitive cellular fitness.

topics.label: Cell of origin and stem cell models in tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the role of normal tissue hierarchies, stemness characteristics, and specific cells of origin in initiating and propagating malignancies such as leukemia and intestinal tumors.

topics.label: Tumor microenvironment, inflammation, and research approaches
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how microenvironmental cues and chronic inflammation promote tumor initiation and maintenance, describe methods to study these cellular interactions, and synthesize the lecture's evolutionary concepts.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture and announces the topic for the following session.
